name: Dimapur
description: Largest city and commercial hub of Nagaland, serving as the primary gateway with the state's only airport and major railway station. Located on the Dhansiri River plains near the Assam border; base for exploring Kachari heritage and nearby nature sites.
facts: Only civil airport and major railhead in Nagaland
On banks of Dhansiri River near Assam border

name: Kachari Ruins (Ruins of Kachari Rajbari)
description: Medieval archaeological site with mushroom-domed sandstone pillars and V-shaped monoliths from the Dimasa Kachari kingdom (pre-13th century). Remnants of the ancient capital, elaborately carved with motifs; ASI protected and a key heritage attraction in the town center.
facts: Ancient capital of Dimasa Kachari kingdom
Behind Naga Shopping Arcade / near Circuit House

name: Dimapur Jain Temple
description: Historic Digambara Jain temple established in 1947, featuring intricate glass work and dedicated to Lord Mahavira. Built by non-Naga Jain settlers who relocated from Kohima during WWII; a prominent spiritual landmark in the city.
facts: On Jain Temple Road near SD Jain School

name: Nagaland Science Centre
description: Interactive science museum behind Naga Shopping Arcade with galleries on senses, children's exhibits, and fun science, plus a planetarium (Taramandal). Promotes scientific awareness; popular family attraction with nominal entry.
facts: Galleries: Our Senses, Children's Corner, Fun Science
Near Kachari Ruins and Super Market

name: Green Park
description: Landscaped recreational park within the State Horticulture Nursery at 4th Mile, featuring greenery, boating, ziplining, kids' activities, and picnic spots. Family-friendly oasis with adventure elements.
facts: Located at 4th/5th Mile in Horticulture Nursery
Popular for picnics and family outings

name: Nagaland Zoological Park
description: State's largest zoo spanning 176 hectares at Rangapahar, focused on Northeast Indian fauna including hornbills, hoolock gibbon, and tigers. Part of Rangapahar Wildlife Sanctuary area; inaugurated 2008. Note: now in Chümoukedima district.

name: Triple Falls (Seithekima)
description: Three-stream waterfall cascading about 280 feet into a natural pool near Seithekima village. Surrounded by lush forest; popular for picnics and short treks. Note: village area now associated with Chümoukedima district.

name: Diezephe Craft Village
description: Artisan village known for traditional Naga woodcarving, bamboo/cane work, and loinloom weaving. Features craft museum, workshops, and homestays; promoted for cultural tourism. Note: now in Chümoukedima district.
facts: Experts in wood carving, weaving, bamboo

name: NEZCC Stone Garden and Museum
description: North East Zone Cultural Centre complex with stone sculpture garden (31 sculptures by Indian artists), traditional morungs, amphitheater, and Northeast Heritage Museum showcasing crafts from eight NE states. Near airport.
facts: About 3 km from railway station, near airport

name: Hong Kong Market
description: Bustling flea market in central Dimapur known for imported goods, clothing, electronics, and local Naga handicrafts. Vibrant shopping hub popular with locals and visitors exploring the commercial gateway.
facts: Mix of local Naga crafts and imported items
Near railway station and city center
